findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` has no optional chaining, so booking with a Google Meet location crashes with a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or [] (organizer has no destination calendar; confirm/payment handlers pass []), where it used to fall back to Cal Video.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Non-calendar (video) references now get `credentialId: undefined`, where they used to get result.credentialId; handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings whose reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are silently left behind on cancel.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365 createEvent always uses the first host's destination externalId, so a collective host after the first posts to another host's calendar id with their own token; the call fails, createEvent swallows the error, and the booking still reports success.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:161 — CalDAV createEvent filters calendars by the first host's externalId, so for any other collective host no calendar matches, nothing is written, and it still returns a success result that gets stored as a reference (silent pass).

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark createEvent/createAttendees use the first host's calendarId regardless of which credential is calling, so a non-first collective host's event goes to the wrong or an inaccessible calendar and fails silently.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — Unrelated logic inversion: slug is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true (it used to be set only when billing was disabled), so billed orgs claim the slug before payment and non-billed orgs get no slug.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — If neither the eventType nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, `?.push` does nothing, and every other collective host's calendar is silently dropped, so the fix does nothing in that case.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — When eventType.destinationCalendar is set, the organizer's own destination is skipped while each other host's is appended; if that calendar belongs to another host, that host gets a duplicate event and the organizer gets none.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175 — Confirm (and the Stripe/PayPal payment-success handlers) rebuild destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar (the first host), so collective events that need confirmation or payment still create a calendar event for only one host.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The fallback `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never matches; update then sends calendarId undefined and delete (line 317) goes to "primary" and 404s silently, orphaning events whose reference lacks externalCalendarId.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — The hangout-link patch still passes `selectedCalendar`, which can now be undefined when no destination matches the credentialId (the insert uses `|| "primary"`), so the patch rejects unhandled and the Meet link never reaches the description.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — Destinations without a credentialId (legacy) go to every organizer credential of that integration with no externalId; Google then writes to "primary" instead of the chosen calendar, the reference loses externalCalendarId, and a collective host's destination creates a duplicate in the organizer's calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — updateLocation now writes calendar references with externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined (updateEvent returns neither); editLocation appends these, so later cancel/reschedule iterate duplicate references without credentials and hit the wrong calendar or fail.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — When merging into newBookingId (seats), only the first old calendar reference is deleted via find(), so the other collective hosts' old calendar events are orphaned.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:208 — Now that a booking has several same-type calendar references (one per host), request-reschedule deletes all of them with the organizer's credential from credentialsMap; other hosts' events 404 and are silently left behind.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:151 — Each collective host's Google insert carries its own conference createRequest, so each host's event can get a separate Meet link, while only the first google_calendar result's hangoutLink goes to attendees.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — console.error(message) was removed from the updateAllCalendarEvents catch, so update failures (such as a credential DB lookup error) are swallowed with no log while the message is built and then unused.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:761 — The loadUsers rewrite turns an empty or invalid dynamicUserList (a plain Error) into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", and drops `organization.slug` from the dynamic-user select even though IsFixedAwareUser requires it.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changes from object to array and is spread into webhook payloads (handleNewBooking.ts:1755 `...evt`), breaking existing webhook subscribers with no versioning or compat shim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` has no optional chaining, so booking with a Google Meet location crashes with a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or [] (organizer has no destination calendar; confirm/payment handlers pass []), where it used to fall back to Cal Video.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Non-calendar (video) references now get `credentialId: undefined`, where they used to get result.credentialId; handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings whose reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are silently left behind on cancel.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavioral change in `packages/core/EventManager.ts` where, in the reference-building return object, `credentialId` is now set to `undefined` for non-calendar integrations (`credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`), whereas it previously used `result.credentialId`. However, the finding’s claimed impact (“handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings whose reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are left behind”) is not verifiable from the provided diff: the shown `handleCancelBooking` changes only process `*_calendar` references (filtering `reference.type.includes("_calendar")`) and do not show any video-meeting deletion logic or any dependency on `credentialId` for video references. Therefore the asserted regression about silently leaving Zoom/Daily meetings behind cannot be confirmed from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365 createEvent always uses the first host's destination externalId, so a collective host after the first posts to another host's calendar id with their own token; the call fails, createEvent swallows the error, and the booking still reports success.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for collective team events, appends additional hosts' destination calendars (`handleNewBooking.ts` pushes `teamDestinationCalendars` onto `evt.destinationCalendar`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` still derives the events URL from only the first element: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` for `/me/calendars/{id}/events`. That means when creating events for later hosts, Office365 will still target the first host's calendar ID (or the organizer's), which can cause posting to the wrong calendar / failing with the wrong token. The finding’s core issue (always using the first host’s destination externalId) is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:161 — CalDAV createEvent filters calendars by the first host's externalId, so for any other collective host no calendar matches, nothing is written, and it still returns a success result that gets stored as a reference (silent pass).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` the CalDAV/iCal create path now destructures only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and filters the available calendars to only those whose `externalId` matches that first element. With the diff changing `destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` looping over multiple destinations/credentials, calls to CalDAV createEvent for non-primary (e.g., other collective hosts) will still see the *first* destination calendar (likely the organizer’s) and may filter to zero calendars for that credential, resulting in `Promise.all([])` (no event creation) rather than creating on the intended calendar. The finding’s “silent pass/success reference stored” part isn’t fully verifiable without the rest of `createEvent` return logic, but the core mismatch/empty-create behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark createEvent/createAttendees use the first host's calendarId regardless of which credential is calling, so a non-first collective host's event goes to the wrong or an inaccessible calendar and fails silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `createEvent` and `createAttendees` now derive `calendarId` from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:758 — The new loadUsers catch sends raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError messages back to the unauthenticated booker as a 400 response, leaking internal DB error details.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, the new `loadUsers` wraps the Prisma query in a `try/catch` and, on `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError`, throws `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` silently does nothing when the organizer has no destination calendar (evt value is null), so other collective hosts' calendars are dropped; no test covers a host without a destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,` around the shown change). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code tries to add other hosts’ destination calendars via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped and never reach downstream calendar creation logic. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — The new multi-destination create loop (one event per host, credential looked up by id with a Prisma DB fallback, and the legacy branch with no credentialId) has no unit tests for multi-host collective bookings or for a credential missing from both memory and the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Non-calendar (video) references now always get `credentialId: undefined` instead of `result.credentialId`, a silent regression that no test asserting referencesToCreate would catch.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the reference object built for each integration result changed from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. This means when `isCalendarType` is false (e.g., video/meeting integrations), `credentialId` is now always `undefined` whereas previously it preserved `result.credentialId`, which is a functional behavior change/regression visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — The legacy destination branch (no credentialId) calls createEvent without an externalId, so references lose externalCalendarId, and Google's credentialId lookup falls back to "primary" instead of the configured calendar; nothing tests this path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within `createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `event.destinationCalendar`, the branch where `destination.credentialId` is falsy calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing an `externalId` (`destination.externalId`). After this diff, `EventManager` stores `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId` (not from `evt.destinationCalendar`), so this path will produce references with `externalCalendarId: undefined`. Additionally, `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` now selects the calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match exists; with no `credentialId` on the destination entries, it will not match and will use `primary` even if a destination `externalId` exists. This is a concrete behavior regression visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — In updateAllCalendarEvents, if a reference's credential is in neither calendarCredentials nor the DB (or has no app slug), `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is still pushed; the multi-reference reschedule path has no test.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the new multi-reference loop in `updateAllCalendarEvents` pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)` even when `credential` is still undefined. Specifically, inside `if (reference.credentialId)`, it tries `this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0]`, then optionally fetches from DB, but regardless of whether either lookup succeeded it executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));`. If the credential isn’t found in memory and either isn’t found in DB or lacks `app.slug` (so `credential` never gets assigned), `updateEvent` is called with `undefined`, which is a real correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-cancel branch now sits inside the per-reference loop, so for a collective booking with N references it deletes events N times across only the organizer's credentials and never uses the other hosts' credentials; neither the multi-host cancel nor the DB credential fallback is tested.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts the recurring-delete path is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (i.e., per calendar reference). In that recurring branch it builds `promises` from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))`, ignoring the current `reference.credentialId`/DB-fetched credential entirely. Therefore, if there are N `_calendar` references (e.g., collective/multi-calendar), the same organizer-credential deletion loop runs N times (duplicate deletes) and it never uses the other references' credentials in the recurring path. This is a concrete behavioral/correctness issue introduced by the refactor to multiple references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match (dead code, same at line 317); a test of update/delete without externalCalendarId would have exposed this.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` introduce fallback logic that cannot work as written. `updateEvent` sets `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — but the `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` to a falsy value (likely `undefined/null`), which will almost never match a real calendar externalId. The same pattern exists in `deleteEvent` (`calendarId` computed the same way). This makes the fallback effectively dead code and likely causes updates/deletes without `externalCalendarId` to fall back incorrectly (e.g., to default/primary) rather than the intended destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365, Lark and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts) always use destinationCalendar[0] rather than the entry matching their credential, so in a mixed-provider collective event the second host's event targets the first host's calendar id; there is no mixed-provider test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over each destination, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` but still passes the same `event` object containing the full destinationCalendar array. Unlike GoogleCalendarService (which selects the calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) and Lark (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) (and CalDAV/BaseCalendarService in `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and use only that first entry to choose the target calendar ID/URL. This will mis-target events when multiple destination calendars are present (e.g., collective/team events), potentially creating/updating/deleting against the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — Only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was changed to `[]`, while BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED (lines 119, 373) still expect `null`; this pins inconsistent payload shapes across code paths, and no e2e test covers a collective event with multiple destination calendars.
